Chapter Fourteen: What Remains
As the centuries roll by, the marks we leave behind slowly fade... but they never quite vanish. Think about it—ruined cities, scattered pieces of art, the scars etched into the earth—they all become threads in the world’s ongoing story. The things we built to last? Sure, they might still be standing, but time and nature reshape them in ways we never imagined.
Imagine a wanderer, hundreds of years after we’re gone. They’d see a world that’s both familiar and strange. Roads and buildings might still outline the landscape, but trees and grass would soften their edges, blurring where human hands once held sway. And if you looked closer, you’d find the everyday objects—bottles, tools, maybe a forgotten toy—hidden beneath layers of soil, just waiting for someone to stumble across them.
The world without us isn’t just empty space. It’s more like a palimpsest—a canvas with layers of memory, loss, and renewal written on top of each other. Our story is woven into the land itself, into the water and the air, blending with the rhythms of life that keep on going.
Most of us don’t realize just how deeply the world is shaped by the things we leave behind. When people are gone, it’s not the end. It’s a transformation. Life finds a way to move forward, adapting and changing, building new stories from the pieces of the old. And maybe that’s the most powerful legacy of all.
